1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by comparing the hashed token stored in the session.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because it is session-bound and hashed.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after a password reset (session.recoveryGrantUntil is cleared, and authenticated is set).

4.why: The website enforces HTTPS with TLS (certs are required, and the server will not start without them).

5.why: Reset codes are hashed using SHA-256, and user data is not stored in plaintext (Argon2id is used for passwords).

6.why: Email messages do not expose private user data (simulated logs show only test tokens, not real data).

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is validated with strict regex and length checks (safeEmail, strongPassword).

8.why: Redirect links are not used; the frontend uses hash-based navigation, and no outgoing URLs are followed.

9.why: Email templates are not dynamically generated from user input; simulated logs use textContent, not innerHTML.

10.why: Error pages and logs do not expose private information or tokens (generic messages are returned).

11.why: Passwords and secret codes are stored securely (Argon2id for passwords, SHA-256 for tokens) and not hardcoded.

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials; all sessions and tokens are randomly generated.

13.why: The system bars users after MAX_ATTEMPTS (5) within RATE_WINDOW_MS (60,000ms).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (generic response for all requests).

15.why: The password reset code is random (randomValue(32)), complex (base64-like), and user-specific (session-bound).
